findings.title: D-A-STUDY (Murphy 32x82) casing head and legs stop 0.75in lower than the note's 78in AFF: head bottom 77.25in above the finished floor

evidence.measured: Resolved casing: legs z 241.5..318.75in (77.25in), head bottom 318.75in. Note and CLAUDE.md say the head bottom is 1/2in below the 78 1/2in body top, i.e. 78.0in AFF (319.5in). head_z = wall.base_ref_z (240.0) + opening.sill_m (0.75, the oak finish) + head_rise (78.5 - 0.5 = 78.0) = 318.75, so the 0.75in oak finish is counted as sill and the product's 78.5in body is measured from the subfloor datum 240.75 while the RO is published 'from the finished floor' (RO top 323.5 = 241.5 + 82). Milling row 'door casing red-oak 3 pcs, longest 77.2in' inherits it (should be 78.0). Low confidence: depends on whether the delivered unit stands on the finished floor or the subfloor.
evidence.expected: Head bottom 78.0in above the finished floor (z 319.5in), legs 78.0in, or the note changed to say 77 1/4in.
